AVOIDING THE WRONG COMPARISON

Start With The Exact Model Before Looking At Age

Size and style both affect the comparison. An 0-15, 2-17, 0-17 and 00-17 shouldn’t be combined under one “mahogany Martin” estimate. Record the stamp exactly and photograph it clearly. If the impression is faint, change the lighting angle before deciding whether an extra zero is present.

The same caution applies to small and scarce versions. A 5-17 or a small-run 000-17 needs a matching model row and evidence for its production identity. Rarity alone doesn’t establish a usable price. Original condition, repair needs and the pool of buyers interested in that configuration still matter.

For a guitar with a missing or uncertain stamp, provide body measurements, the neck joint, bridge and headstock. A provisional identification should remain provisional in the valuation. Choosing an attractive price first and fitting the guitar to that category afterwards creates avoidable uncertainty.

Four-string tenors belong in the Martin tenor price guide, while plectrum models have their own value comparisons. Modern 000-15M, 00-15M and 000-17 instruments aren’t included in these vintage rows.
